- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 82.5), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-period, model underreacts; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not exceed prior 5-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 3-day sentiment average) to adjust forecast volatility.
